title: Global Gas Turbine Manufacturing Outlook: Crunch, for Now | BloombergNEF
gist: A bottom-up BloombergNEF database of 44 gas turbine assembly facilities across 26 manufacturers shows announced expansions lifting annual output by more than half by 2030, with GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries raising their combined share from ~66% to ~70%; the binding constraints have moved upstream of final assembly, and BNEF warns today's scarcity could invert into overcapacity if AI-driven power demand softens.

themes.theme: Capacity expansion and the boom-bust warning

insights.claim: BloombergNEF's bottom-up database of 44 gas turbine assembly facilities across 26 manufacturers shows announced expansions lifting annual global output by more than half by 2030.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: A >50% supply increase by 2030 sets a clock on today's pricing power for turbine OEMs — order backlogs, not capacity, are the durable asset.
insights.quote: BloombergNEF’s bottom-up database of 44 assembly facilities across 26 manufacturers shows announced expansions lifting annual output by more than half by 2030.

insights.claim: Strong demand has stretched global gas turbine manufacturing capacity, lengthening delivery times for advanced machines.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Long lead times are a direct schedule risk for gas-fired projects underwriting data center power — watch delivery slots, not just orders.
insights.locator: Strong demand has stretched gas turbine manufacturing capacity

insights.claim: The current gas turbine scarcity does not rule out oversupply later, as the industry has a documented history of booms and busts producing plant closures, supply chain consolidation and bankruptcies.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: The consensus scarcity trade has an explicit reversal path; size positions in turbine names for cycle risk, not secular growth.
insights.quote: Today’s scarcity does not rule out oversupply tomorrow.
insights.locator: Today’s scarcity does not rule out oversupply tomorrow

insights.claim: Three specific triggers could push gas turbine manufacturing back toward underused plants: softer AI-driven power demand, slipping construction readiness, or competition from cheaper batteries.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete three-item watchlist for timing an exit from the turbine capex cycle — battery cost curves are the least-watched of the three.
insights.quote: Softer AI-driven power demand, slipping construction readiness or competition from cheaper batteries could push the industry back toward underused plants.
insights.locator: Softer AI-driven power demand, slipping construction readiness

insights.claim: The demand outlook for gas turbine manufacturing is explicitly conditional rather than assured, with BloombergNEF framing the current crunch as temporary in its own headline judgement.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: A research house calling the crunch temporary is a soft contrarian signal against extrapolating current turbine pricing into terminal value.
insights.quote: However, if power demand softens, today’s scarcity could become tomorrow’s overcapacity.

themes.theme: Big three consolidation via brownfield expansion

insights.claim: GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries control about 66% of global gas turbine manufacturing capacity today, rising to roughly 70% by 2030.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Market structure is tightening rather than fragmenting during a boom — pricing power should persist for the big three even as volumes expand.
insights.locator: GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries control about 66%

insights.claim: The three largest turbine makers supply 28GW of the 35GW of capacity added to 2030, almost all of it from expansions at existing plants rather than new greenfield sites.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Brownfield-only expansion means lower capex intensity and faster reversibility — incumbents can add supply without stranding large new assets.
insights.quote: almost all of it from expansions at existing plants rather than new greenfield sites
insights.locator: They supply 28GW of the 35GW added over that period

insights.claim: Manufacturers outside the big three hold about a third of global gas turbine capacity today but supply only roughly 20% of new capacity additions to 2030, meaning they lose relative share through the cycle.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Smaller turbine makers are being out-invested during the upcycle — a structural share-loss story that screens against second-tier exposure.
insights.locator: Manufacturers outside the big three hold about a third

insights.claim: Among smaller players, Caterpillar's Solar Turbines expands capacity by close to 80%, Doosan Enerbility more than doubles on the back of US orders, and Baker Hughes and Ansaldo Energia each expand assembly lines by 28%.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Doosan Enerbility's doubling is the highest-beta expansion in the set and is explicitly levered to US orders — the most exposed name if US demand slips.
insights.quote: Doosan Enerbility more than doubles on the back of US orders
insights.locator: Caterpillar’s Solar Turbines expands by close to 80%

themes.theme: Turbine class mix favours heavy-frame scale

insights.claim: Heavy-frame turbines account for almost four-fifths of capacity additions, growing 59% and lifting their share of global capacity to 72% by 2030.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Supply is being built for large baseload-scale projects, so smaller distributed gas projects will stay supply-constrained longest.
insights.locator: Heavy-frame turbines take up almost four-fifths of the additions

insights.claim: The heavy-frame skew is driven by utilities and data center-linked projects buying for scale and efficiency.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Confirms AI data center load is now shaping physical manufacturing mix in heavy industry, not just electricity demand forecasts.
insights.quote: as utilities and data center-linked projects buy for scale and efficiency
insights.locator: growing 59% and lifting their share to 72% by 2030

insights.claim: Industrial turbines grow only 41% and aeroderivatives 39%, held back by upstream bottlenecks and by competition from aerospace, oil and gas, and defense sectors for the same parts.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Cross-sector parts competition means aerospace and defense order books are a leading indicator for aeroderivative turbine availability and price.
insights.quote: held back by upstream bottlenecks and competition from aerospace, oil and gas and defense sectors for same parts

themes.theme: Bottleneck has moved upstream of assembly

insights.claim: The limiting factors for gas turbine delivery now lie in the stages preceding final assembly, so headline assembly-capacity expansion overstates real deliverable supply.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Announced assembly expansions are a misleading supply metric — underwrite turbine availability on component suppliers instead.
insights.quote: The limiting factors for turbine delivery now lie in the stages preceding final assembly.
insights.locator: The limiting factors for turbine delivery

insights.claim: The industry has flagged eight specific upstream constraints on turbine output: single-crystal blades and vanes, structural forgings, specialty alloys, rare-earth feedstock, generators, controls, heat recovery steam generators, and skilled labor.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: A ready-made supplier watchlist — forgings, specialty alloys and rare-earth feedstock are the chokepoints where pricing power actually sits.
insights.quote: single-crystal blades and vanes, structural forgings, specialty alloys, rare-earth feedstock, generators, controls, heat recovery steam generators, and skilled labor
insights.locator: Capacity depends on upstream suppliers keeping pace
